question: Refer to the exhibit. An engineer must configure port security on a Cisco Nexus 5000 Series Switch to meet these requirements: only VSAN 10 devices are permitted; a specific pWWN must be permitted only through san-port-channel 2; any WWN must be permitted through fc1/1-3; and auto-learning must be disabled. Which configuration meets these requirements?
options: port-security database vsan 10 / pwwn 20:10:10:10:10:10:10:10 interface san-port-channel 2 / any wwn interface fc1/1-3 / port-security commit vsan 10
port-security database vsan 10 / pwwn 20:10:10:10:10:10:10:10 interface fc1/1-3 / any wwn interface san-port-channel 2 / port-security commit vsan 10
port-security database vsan 10 / pwwn 20:10:10:10:10:10:10:10 interface san-port-channel 2 / any wwn interface fc1/1-3 / port-security auto-learn vsan 10
port-security database vsan 1 / pwwn 20:10:10:10:10:10:10:10 interface san-port-channel 2 / any wwn interface fc1/1-3 / port-security commit vsan 10
theory: Manual port-security database configuration scopes entries per VSAN with port-security database vsan 10, then binds a specific device pWWN to a single interface (interface san-port-channel 2) while a broader any-wwn interface fc1/1-3 entry allows any device through that separate port range, exactly matching the stated per-interface restrictions; committing with port-security commit vsan 10 saves the database. Because auto-learning is off by default until explicitly enabled, this manual method inherently satisfies the 'auto-learning must be disabled' requirement without extra commands. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 20 - Port Security, Manual Database Configuration)
